{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The deciding factor is the 90-day window. A names a specific affiliated customer pair, a Wisconsin public adjuster and roofing contractor, with a documented narrow pain (manual intake, inconsistent claim documentation). B has no identified prospect at all.",
    "A's willingness to pay is anchored to the same buyer type. ClaimWizard ($99/$250/mo), claimOS ($199 + $99/user), Claim Titan ($82.50/user) and AdjustCRM ($65/user) all publish pricing for public adjusting firms. So the price hypothesis is grounded for the exact payer, not just the category.",
    "A's demand evidence includes a named operations director at a public adjusting firm describing the manual-process pain (Pipedrive case study). It also includes a small public adjuster asking for a simple claims CRM, which matches the intake-only scope.",
    "B's acquisition evidence works against a 90-day goal. The cited SEO channel has a 7-month payback and $480–942 CAC. The cheaper community channel has no sourced cost.",
    "B's own brief says the market is shrinking. Google downgraded dynamic rendering to a 'workaround, not a long-term solution' in favor of SSR/SSG frameworks. The brief also lists 7+ competitors starting at $5/mo with low switching costs.",
    "A has real weaknesses: only 188 in-state licensees, 5+ incumbents with AI extraction, and Wisconsin data-security compliance work. These mostly limit how far the business can scale. They do not block landing one paying customer within 90 days, which is the actual question."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's acquisition-channel evidence. The CAC/ROI/payback figures are generic B2B SaaS SEO statistics from a marketing blog, not data on prerendering services. Their 7-month payback is incompatible with a 90-day first-customer goal. The only faster channel (developer-community engagement) is explicitly marked [unsourced] for cost, so it counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's edge rests largely on the named customer, but the brief's own open questions admit that commitment may be informal. A's AdjustEdge pricing could not be re-verified. A's second acquisition channel (roofing lead ads) targets homeowners, not the software payer. Wisconsin breach-notification obligations could delay live use of claimant data. If the customer relationship is not real, A collapses toward B's position: a crowded niche with no warm lead."
}
